What is meant is Satan, named by the verbal noun as if he were whispering in himself, because whispering is his craft and his occupation to which he devotes himself. Or what is intended is the one possessing the whispering. We have already discussed with him his claim that al-zilzal with a fatha is a noun and with a kasra is a verbal noun in ﴿When the earth is shaken [al-zilzal]﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 1]. In ﴿who﴾ (alladhi) it is permissible to read it in the genitive as an attribute, or in the nominative and accusative by way of dispraise (al-shatm). The ﴿min﴾ in ﴿of the jinn and of mankind﴾ is partitive, meaning: being of the jinn and of mankind. It is then in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning that this whisperer is part of the jinn and part of mankind. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is also permissible for ﴿min﴾ to be connected to "whispers" (yuwaswisu), meaning the starting point of the action, i.e., he whispers in their breasts from the direction of the jinn and from the direction of mankind. End of quotation.

Since the harm to the religion, which is the affliction of whispering, is greater than the harm to the world, however great that may be, the seeking of refuge from it was built upon three attributes: the Lord, the King and the God, even though the object sought is one. In seeking refuge from three things (the darkening one, the blowers in knots, and the envier), one attribute is used, which is the Lord, even though the things sought refuge from are many.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ), when he went to his bed, would join his palms, blow into them, and recite: "Say: He is God, One" and the two refuge surahs. Then he would wipe with them whatever he could of his body, beginning with his head and face and what faced him of his body, doing this three times. (May God bless him, honour him, glorify him, ennoble him and bless his family and companions, possessors of generosity, with abundant peace.)
